quote: Gegeben ist eine rationale Funktion R von U und z. Man soll eine rationale Funk- tion mit reellen Coefficienten von $U, U' = \frac{dU}{dz}, U'', \ldots$ und z bestimmen, welche in sich übergeht, wenn man $U = R(U, z)$ setzt.
english: Given a rational function R of U and z. One is to determine a rational function with real coefficients of U, U' = dU/dz, U'', ... and z that is transformed into itself when one sets U = R(U, z).
topic: Notes posing several problems: expanding e^π = i^i into a simple continued fraction, a reduction of a problem of Lindemann's to finding rational functions invariant under a substitution, the meaning of Jacobi's inversion problem and Abel's theorem for genus p = ∞, and the behaviour of the second root when a root is approximated by a quadratic equation.

triage.modern_statement: Take a rational function R(U,z) and the substitution U ↦ R(U,z), where U = U(z) is an unknown function. Extend the substitution to derivatives by the chain rule: U' ↦ dR(U,z)/dz, and so on. This is the prolongation of the map to the jet space with coordinates (z, U, U', U'', ...). The question is to find a rational differential function Φ(z, U, U', ..., U^(n)) with real coefficients that this prolonged map leaves unchanged, i.e. Φ∘(prolonged R) = Φ. In modern terms: find a non-constant element of the fixed field of the prolonged rational self-map on jet space, i.e. a rational differential invariant of the substitution. The classical model case is the Schwarzian derivative. It is unchanged under Möbius substitutions U ↦ (aU+b)/(cU+d) with constant coefficients. The note says this is a reduction of some 'problem of Lindemann's', but the page does not say which one, and I could not identify it.
triage.answered_by: No specific answer to this note was found. Related modern work exists: the theory of differential rational invariants (Lie–Tresse theory, invariants of algebraic groups acting on differential fields) and the study of invariant rational functions under dominant rational self-maps (Bell–Moosa–Satriano, Selecta Math. 2024; Bell–Moosa–Topaz on invariant hypersurfaces and D-constant rational functions). None of these sources mentions Hilbert's note or Lindemann's problem.

evidence.claim: The Schwarzian derivative is invariant under Möbius transformations. This is the classical example of a rational differential expression in U, U', U'', U''' that is unchanged by a rational substitution in U.

Modern work studies, for an algebraic variety X with a dominant rational self-map φ, invariant rational functions f, i.e. elements of the fixed field Fix(k(X), φ*). It introduces the 'stabilised algebraic dimension' and shows that if some cartesian power of (X,φ) has a nonconstant invariant rational function, then the second power already does. Applied to the jet-space prolongation of U ↦ R(U,z), this framework covers Hilbert's question in general form.

Bell, Moosa and Topaz link rational dynamics with differential/D-operators. If a system has infinitely many totally invariant hypersurfaces, then a nonconstant invariant rational function (D-constant) exists.
There is work on the field of differential rational invariants of subgroups of the affine group acting on ordinary differential fields. This is the differential-algebra setting of Hilbert's question.

Hilbert's 23 problems include the 14th problem on finite generation of rings of invariants. That problem is about polynomial invariants of algebraic group actions, not differential invariants of a single rational substitution, so this note is not one of the published problems.

triage.why: The note is clear enough to restate precisely: find a rational differential invariant of a rational substitution U ↦ R(U,z) prolonged to derivatives. It is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem. I found no source that discusses this note, names the 'problem of Lindemann's' it is supposed to reduce, or claims to answer this exact question. The nearby modern areas are the Schwarzian derivative and Möbius invariance, differential invariants (Lie–Tresse theory), and invariant rational functions of rational self-maps (Bell–Moosa–Satriano 2024; Bell–Moosa–Topaz). They give general tools and criteria for when invariants exist, but none is shown to be a resolution of Hilbert's specific question. That fixed fields of prolonged maps are the right formulation is my own interpretation; no source connects them to Hilbert. Calling it solved would go beyond what the sources support, so 'possibly_unexplored' with low confidence is the most honest label. Research on invariant rational functions under rational maps is ongoing (2023–2024 papers), but whether anyone is working on Hilbert's specific question is unknown, hence 'unclear'.
